q: Does the Q^2Chemistry platform maintain accuracy on strongly-correlated systems (e.g. Cr2, N2 near dissociation, transition-metal dimers) where UCCSD/UCCSD-family ansatze are known to break down?
basis: The paper's H2/Fig 6 sanity check exercises a trivially-complete regime (UCCSD spans the full CI space for H2/STO-3G, so the machine-precision agreement is analytically expected). The Cr2 demo (C3) targets a strongly-correlated system but only reports MPS wall-clock scaling on 768 cores, not energy accuracy vs. an exact (e.g. DMRG) reference. Whether the platform's ansatze deliver chemical accuracy in the multireference regime is not established by the paper's own results.
next_steps: Run Q^2Chemistry on N2 across the dissociation curve (0.9-2.5 A) with UCCSD, k-UpCCGSD, and ADAPT-VQE ansatze, comparing to CASSCF(10,8)/DMRG reference. Free-endpoint feasible: use PySCF+OpenFermion (STO-3G/6-31G) for the classical-simulator side, plus a DMRG reference via block2 (open-source). Target: report max energy error and non-parallelism error (NPE) across the curve for each ansatz.

q: How does Q^2Chemistry's MPS backend interact with modern quantum error mitigation (ZNE, PEC, virtual distillation) - does the platform expose hooks for QEM at the circuit level, and how much of the reported near-FCI accuracy survives a realistic noise model?
basis: The paper presents noiseless MPS simulations; there is no reported integration with QEM techniques and no benchmark under a hardware-realistic noise channel. Modern quantum-chemistry workflows on real hardware (2024-2026 IBM/Quantinuum/IonQ papers) are dominated by mitigation choices, so a platform's utility for actual hardware runs depends heavily on this integration.
next_steps: Instrument an H2/LiH VQE run through the platform (or a functional-equivalent OpenFermion+Mitiq stack if Q^2Chemistry source is not obtainable) with a depolarizing + amplitude-damping noise model calibrated to a modern superconducting device. Sweep ZNE (Richardson extrapolation, orders 1-3) and virtual distillation, and report residual energy error vs. FCI as a function of two-qubit gate error rate. Compare to Mitiq baseline.

q: How does the platform perform on catalytically-relevant or drug-relevant benchmark molecules (e.g. FeMoco active site, cytochrome P450 iron center, or a small drug-fragment like caffeine) - i.e. molecules where quantum-chemistry-on-QC is actually pitched as delivering value?
basis: The paper's numerical demos are H2 (Fig 6) and bulk silicon bands (Fig 7). Neither is a target where near-term quantum chemistry is expected to outperform classical methods. Whether the platform's ansatz + MPS backend combination is competitive on the systems the field actually cares about (metal catalysts, active sites, drug fragments) is untested in the paper.
next_steps: Select a canonical near-term-QC benchmark set (e.g. Fe(II)-porphyrin CAS(32,34), Mn3O4 model cluster, active-space Hamiltonians from the OpenFermion benchmark suite). Run VQE-UCCSD and ADAPT-VQE at CAS-projected reduced qubit counts (10-16 qubits, tractable on state-vector), compare energies to DMRG/CASPT2 reference. Report parameter counts, iteration counts, and energy error.

q: How noise-robust is the integrated Q^2Chemistry pipeline end-to-end (Hamiltonian generation to VQE energy) - i.e. do errors from finite-shot sampling, gate noise, and readout error compound catastrophically or does the platform's design absorb them gracefully?
basis: The paper reports noiseless simulator results; there is no analysis of how the classical-quantum interface (Hamiltonian construction, measurement grouping, parameter update loop) behaves when the quantum backend returns finite-shot noisy estimates. This is a critical property for any platform that will be used with real hardware.
next_steps: For H2/STO-3G and LiH/STO-3G, run the VQE loop with a shot-noise backend at N_shots in {100, 1000, 10000, 100000} and a depolarizing gate error in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}. Report VQE energy variance across 20 seeds per configuration, plus optimizer convergence rate. Compare against a canonical Qiskit-Nature VQE with the same noise model.

q: Would ML-driven ansatz selection (e.g. an RL agent or a supervised model over molecular graph features) reduce the parameter count / circuit depth of Q^2Chemistry ansatze compared to hand-crafted symmetry-reduced UCCSD, without sacrificing accuracy?
basis: The paper reports 53 variational parameters for its symmetry-reduced UCCSD on H2/ccj-pVDZ - substantial for a two-electron system. ADAPT-VQE and other adaptive schemes already prune parameters heuristically; whether a learned model over molecule descriptors can do better, and how it interacts with the Q^2Chemistry platform's ansatz-builder interface, is unexplored in the paper.
next_steps: Train a small RL agent (e.g. PPO with a graph-neural-network state encoder over molecule + operator pool) to select excitation operators one at a time, using accuracy-vs-FCI as reward and circuit-depth as penalty. Baseline: hand-crafted UCCSD and standard ADAPT-VQE. Molecule set: H2, LiH, BeH2, H4-chain (STO-3G, tractable). Report Pareto front of (parameter count, energy error) and compare to the paper's 53-parameter figure.
